title: Time Intelligence, Statistics, Semi-Additive Measures and Calculation Groups

header.html: Implement time intelligence measures; Use basic statistical functions; Create semi-additive measures; Create calculation groups
the official PL-300 study guide (skills measured as of April 20, 2026)

html:
1Time intelligence measures

Time intelligence compares and accumulates values over dates: year to date, the same period last year, rolling windows. These functions need a proper date table: one row per day, no gaps, marked as the date table and related to the fact table (see Module 5). Always pass the date column of the Date table, never the date column of the fact table.

Function What it does
TOTALYTD Year-to-date total of an expression; a shortcut for CALCULATE with DATESYTD
DATESYTD, DATESQTD, DATESMTD Return the dates from the start of the year, quarter or month up to the last date in context; used inside CALCULATE
SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR Shifts the dates in context back exactly one year
DATEADD Shifts the dates by any number of days, months, quarters or years; a negative number goes back
DATESINPERIOD Returns the dates of a period from a start date; used for rolling windows such as the last three months
PARALLELPERIOD Shifts the period and returns the whole period, so a partial month becomes a full month

The pattern for a prior-period comparison is CALCULATE of the measure with a date-shifting function as the filter. Variables keep the year-over-year change readable and make sure each value is calculated once.

Sales YoY Percent =
VAR CurrentSales = [Total Sales]
VAR PriorSales =
    CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR ( 'Date'[Date] ) )
RETURN
    DIVIDE ( CurrentSales - PriorSales, PriorSales )
Exam tip

. Time intelligence needs a contiguous Date table marked as the date table. Use the date column of that table in the function, or the result is wrong or blank.

Exam tip

. DATEADD shifts the dates you have; PARALLELPERIOD returns the full parallel period. SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR is the same as DATEADD with minus one year.

2Basic statistical functions

Function What it returns
AVERAGE, MIN, MAX The mean, the smallest and the largest value of a column
MEDIAN The middle value of a column
STDEV.S and VAR.S Standard deviation and variance of a sample; STDEV.P and VAR.P are for the whole population
PERCENTILE.INC The value at a percentile from 0 to 1, with both ends included; PERCENTILE.EXC leaves them out
COUNTROWS The number of rows of a table in the current filter context
RANKX The rank of each item by an expression; descending by default, so rank 1 is the highest
TOPN A table of the top N rows by an expression, used inside CALCULATE or an iterator

The aggregation functions take a column and ignore blanks. The X versions, such as MEDIANX and PERCENTILEX.INC, evaluate an expression for each row of a table first. For RANKX, give the table as ALL of the items, for example all product names. Otherwise the filter context leaves one item in each row, and every item gets rank 1.

Exam tip

. STDEV.S and VAR.S are for a sample; STDEV.P and VAR.P are for a full population. RANKX needs ALL around the items to rank against all of them, and TOPN returns a table, not a single number.

3Semi-additive measures

Not every number can be summed across every dimension.

Kind Rule Example
Additive Can be added across all dimensions Sales amount, units sold
Semi-additive Can be added across some dimensions but not across time Account balance, inventory on hand, headcount
Non-additive Cannot be added at all; recompute it from its parts Ratios, percentages

A balance table stores a snapshot per day. If a monthly matrix adds the daily snapshots, the result is far too high. A semi-additive measure uses the last value in the period, and still adds across accounts or products.

Function Use
LASTDATE The last date in the current filter context, even when no data exists on that day
LASTNONBLANK The last date that has a value for an expression; it returns the last known balance
CLOSINGBALANCEMONTH The value on the last date of the month in context; versions exist for the quarter and the year
FIRSTDATE, OPENINGBALANCEMONTH The opening counterparts

The average over time is another valid measure for a snapshot, but it is not the closing balance.

Closing Balance =
CALCULATE ( SUM ( Balance[Amount] ), LASTDATE ( 'Date'[Date] ) )

Last Known Balance =
CALCULATE (
    SUM ( Balance[Amount] ),
    LASTNONBLANK ( 'Date'[Date], CALCULATE ( COUNTROWS ( Balance ) ) )
)
Exam tip

. Never sum a balance or an inventory level over time. Use CALCULATE with LASTDATE, or LASTNONBLANK when the last day may have no row, or CLOSINGBALANCEMONTH.

4Calculation groups

A calculation group is a set of calculation items that change how any measure is calculated. The classic use is time intelligence: one group with the items Current, Year to date and Prior year works for every measure, so you write three items instead of three variants of each measure.

Topic Fact
Create In Model view, choose Calculation group (or use TMDL)
Prerequisite Discourage implicit measures must be turned on; Power BI Desktop asks to change it
Calculation item A DAX expression that uses SELECTEDMEASURE, the measure being evaluated
Applies to Explicit measures only, never implicit ones
Precedence Set in the Properties pane; it decides the order when two groups affect one measure
Dynamic format string A format expression on an item, so a year-over-year item shows a percentage while the others show currency
Benefit Fewer measures: 20 measures and 3 items replace 60 measures

A calculation item for year to date wraps SELECTEDMEASURE in CALCULATE with DATESYTD. To limit an item to some measures, test with ISSELECTEDMEASURE. The group appears in the model as a column that you place on a matrix column area or in a slicer.

Exam tip

. Calculation items use SELECTEDMEASURE, work only on explicit measures, and need Discourage implicit measures turned on. Use precedence when two calculation groups combine, and a dynamic format string to change the format per item.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A matrix must show year-to-date sales by month. The model has a Date table that is marked as the date table. Which function should the measure use?

  • ATOTALYTD over the date column of the Date table
  • BDATESINPERIOD over the Sales table's date column
  • CSAMEPERIODLASTYEAR over the Date table's date column
  • DPARALLELPERIOD over the Sales table's date column
Show the answer

Answer: A. TOTALYTD accumulates the measure from the start of the year, and the other options either shift the period or use the fact table's date column.

S2An Inventory table stores UnitsOnHand once per product per day. A monthly matrix adds the daily values and shows numbers that are far too high. The matrix should show the closing quantity of each month. What should you use?

  • ACALCULATE with the sum of UnitsOnHand and DATESYTD of the Date column
  • BCALCULATE with the sum of UnitsOnHand and ALL on the Date table
  • CCALCULATE with the sum of UnitsOnHand and LASTDATE of the Date column
  • DCALCULATE with the sum of UnitsOnHand and FIRSTDATE of the Date column
Show the answer

Answer: C. A semi-additive measure takes the value on the last date of the period instead of adding values over time.

S3A balance measure uses LASTDATE and returns blank for months whose last day has no row in the table. Which change returns the last known balance of each month?

  • AReplace LASTDATE with DATESYTD over the Date column
  • BReplace LASTDATE with LASTNONBLANK over the Date column
  • CReplace LASTDATE with FIRSTDATE over the Date column
  • DReplace LASTDATE with PARALLELPERIOD over the Date column
Show the answer

Answer: B. LASTNONBLANK returns the last date that actually has data, whereas LASTDATE returns the last date in context even when it is empty.

S4A model has 20 measures. Analysts want a year-to-date, a prior-year and a year-over-year version of each. What is the most efficient way?

  • AWrite 60 separate time intelligence measures
  • BAdd three calculated columns to the Date table
  • CCreate one calculation group with three items
  • DBuild three quick measures and copy them 20 times
Show the answer

Answer: C. One calculation group with three items that use SELECTEDMEASURE applies to all explicit measures without duplicating them.

S5An author starts to create a calculation group in Model view, and Power BI Desktop asks to change a model setting. Which setting is it?

  • ATurn on Assume referential integrity in the model
  • BTurn on Apply security filter in both directions
  • CTurn off Auto date/time for the current file
  • DTurn on Discourage implicit measures in the model
Show the answer

Answer: D. Calculation groups work only with explicit measures, so Discourage implicit measures must be on.

S6A table lists products with their sales. Each row must show the product's rank among all products, with the highest sales ranked first. Which function should the measure use?

  • ATOPN over ALL of the products, using the sales measure
  • BRANKX over ALL of the products, using the sales measure
  • CPERCENTILE.INC over the products, using the sales measure
  • DMEDIANX over ALL of the products, using the sales measure
Show the answer

Answer: B. RANKX returns a rank for each item, and ALL keeps every product in the ranking instead of only the current row.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Which function shifts dates by any number of intervals?

Show the answer

DATEADD.

R2Which function returns the last date that has data?

Show the answer

LASTNONBLANK.

R3Which function inside a calculation item returns the measure being evaluated?

Show the answer

SELECTEDMEASURE.

R4Which function gives the standard deviation of a sample?

Show the answer

STDEV.S.

R5Which function returns the top N rows of a table by an expression?

Show the answer

TOPN.

R6What must a Date table be for time intelligence to work?

Show the answer

Unique, contiguous dates, marked as the date table.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Requirement Contiguous Date table marked as the date table; pass its date column
Year to date TOTALYTD, or CALCULATE with DATESYTD
Prior period SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR, DATEADD (any interval), PARALLELPERIOD (full period)
Rolling window DATESINPERIOD from a start date and a negative number of intervals
Statistics MEDIAN, STDEV.S and VAR.S for a sample, PERCENTILE.INC, RANKX with ALL, TOPN returns a table
Semi-additive Balances and inventory are not summed over time; LASTDATE, LASTNONBLANK, CLOSINGBALANCEMONTH
Calculation group Model view; SELECTEDMEASURE; explicit measures only; Discourage implicit measures; precedence
Format A dynamic format string changes the format per calculation item
